config.title: Recursive TreeView

intro.title: Recursive TreeView
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TreeView component that can display nested data structures, like a folder system, using recursion. You will learn how a React component can call itself to render deeply nested items, which is the core programming concept of recursion. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript interfaces for type-safe data, and conditional rendering. By the end, you will have a working, expandable tree that visually represents hierarchical relationships.
intro.usecase: Recursive TreeView components are essential for displaying hierarchical data structures in modern applications. You'll find them in file explorers like VS Code's sidebar, where folders can contain subfolders and files. They're also used in organizational charts, nested comment threads on platforms like Reddit, and complex navigation menus in admin dashboards. As a developer, implementing recursive TreeViews helps you efficiently render deeply nested data while maintaining clean, reusable component architecture.

objectives: Define a TypeScript interface to represent tree node structure with children property
Apply recursion to traverse nested tree data structures in React components
Implement conditional rendering to display tree nodes only when they exist
Use React props to pass tree node data from parent to child components
Construct a recursive component function that calls itself for nested children
Execute proper TypeScript typing for component props to ensure type safety
Handle click events to toggle visibility of child nodes in the tree
Utilize React state hooks to manage expanded/collapsed node states
Apply array mapping to render multiple child components from node arrays
Return JSX structure that recursively builds the visual tree hierarchy
Control component rendering depth through conditional checks on children
Modify component styling to visually indicate expanded and collapsed states

steps.title: Define TreeNode interface for type safety
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named TreeNode with required properties: id (string), label (string), and an optional children property (array of TreeNode).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define TreeNode interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TreeNode interface that defines the structure for tree nodes with type safety.
successCriteria: The TreeNode interface must have: id (string), label (string), and children? (TreeNode[]).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TreeNode interface with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all required properties (id, label) are present and correctly typed, and children is optional (TreeNode[]).
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode interface is missing or incorrect. Ensure it has id: string, label: string, and children?: TreeNode[].

steps.hint: Define the component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax, and type the props parameter.

successCriteria: The component must be named TreeView, accept a prop called 'nodes' typed as TreeNode[], and return JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TreeView component with properly typed props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component is named TreeView, accepts a 'nodes' prop of type TreeNode[], and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't meet the requirements. Check that you've named it TreeView, typed the nodes prop as TreeNode[], and returned JSX.Element.

steps.hint: Define a new component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to type the props parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new TreeNodeItem component is created with typed props, ready to be used to render individual tree nodes.
successCriteria: Component named TreeNodeItem exists
Accepts a prop called 'node'
Prop is typed as TreeNode
Returns JSX (a div element)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TreeNodeItem component with properly typed props. This component will serve as the building block for rendering each node in our tree.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component: 1) Is named TreeNodeItem, 2) Accepts a 'node' prop, 3) Types the prop as TreeNode, and 4) Returns JSX (like a div).
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNodeItem component wasn't created correctly. Remember to create a new component that accepts a 'node' prop of type TreeNode and returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize expanded state in TreeNodeItem
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, initialize a state variable called 'isExpanded' using useState with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should be typed as boolean.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component should have a state variable 'isExpanded' initialized to false, ready to track whether the node is expanded or collapsed.
successCriteria: useState hook is called
State variable is named 'isExpanded'
Initial value is false
State is typed as boolean
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isExpanded state in TreeNodeItem. This boolean state will track whether each tree node is expanded (children visible) or collapsed (children hidden).
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) Used useState with false as the initial value, 2) Named the state variable 'isExpanded', and 3) Typed it as boolean with useState<boolean>(false).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside TreeNodeItem, you need to call useState(false) to create a boolean state variable named 'isExpanded'. Remember to use the useState hook you imported earlier.

steps.title: Define toggle handler in TreeNodeItem
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, define a function named toggleExpanded that toggles the isExpanded state.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from useState to update the state by inverting the current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component will have a toggleExpanded function that toggles the isExpanded state when called.
successCriteria: The toggleExpanded function is defined, uses setIsExpanded, and correctly toggles the boolean value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggle handler that will control the expanded/collapsed state of tree nodes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function correctly toggles the state. Make sure you're using the state setter function to invert the current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that calls setIsExpanded with the opposite of the current isExpanded value.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering for children
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNodeItem component, add conditional rendering to display the node's children when isExpanded is true and the node has children.
steps.hint: Use a logical AND (&&) operator to conditionally render content. Check if isExpanded is true and if node.children exists and has length.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNodeItem component will include logic to conditionally render child nodes when expanded.
successCriteria: The code includes a conditional check using isExpanded and node.children, and renders content only when both conditions are true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the children. The component will now only show child nodes when the parent is expanded and has children.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the conditional logic might be incomplete. Make sure you're checking both isExpanded and that node.children exists and has content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for children is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the isExpanded state and check if the node has children before rendering them.

steps.hint: When node.children exists and isExpanded is true, call TreeView with the children array.

node.children is passed as the data prop

successCriteria: The code should include a map method on the data array inside the TreeView component's return statement, returning a TreeNodeItem for each node with the correct prop.
